```{r}
#set params
rS = 0.027 #sensitive cell proliferation rate. Hardcoded in paper and all the different params are scaled after this.

rR_coef = 0.75 #Resistant cell prolif rate. paper has 0.5 - 1.0. Maybe use random uniform to pick coeff
d_coef = 0.25 # Death rate for both cell types**
dD = 1.5 # dosage death rate**
K = 1 # tumour carrying cap **
N0 = 0.375 #initial tumour density
R0_coef = 0.05 #resistant cell fraction

#scale the params by r0 and N0 according to paper
rR = rR_coef * rS
d = d_coef * rS
K = 1 
R0 = R0_coef * N0

#Get initial amount of S cells
S0 = N0 * (1-R0_coef)

#starting state
Starting_state = c(S = S0, R = R0)

#time res for segments 
ode_res = 1

#noise param
sigma <- 0.025


```

#get starting state

loop analysis over top 3 patients
```{r}
best_fits <- get_n_best_fits(3)

top_n_sims <- simulate_patients(best_fits)

top_n_sims_long <- top_n_sims |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(PSA_simulated, PSA_observed), values_to= "PSA", names_to = "metric") 

ggplot(top_n_sims_long, aes(x=time, y=PSA, color = metric)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~PatientID)

```



closed-loop simulator vs actual data, top 5 patients
```{r}
best5     <- get_n_best_fits(5)
patients5 <- load_bruchowsky_patients(best5$PatientId)

for (i in 1:nrow(best5)) {
  pid      <- best5$PatientId[i]
  pdat     <- patients5[[as.character(pid)]]
  baseline <- first(pdat$PSA_raw)
  t_max    <- max(pdat$Time)

  pars <- c(rS = 0.027, rR = best5$rR[i], d = best5$dS[i], dD = 1.5, K = 1)
  init <- c(S = best5$S0[i], R = best5$R0[i])

  sim <- simulate_closed_loop(pars, init, baseline, t_max = t_max, meas_sigma = 2)

  #simulated treatment-ON blocks for shading
  blocks <- sim |>
    mutate(seg = consecutive_id(D)) |>
    group_by(seg) |>
    summarise(start = first(time), end = last(time), dose = first(D), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(dose == 1)

  print(
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data = blocks, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
                fill = "grey75", alpha = 0.5) +
      geom_line(data = sim, aes(time, PSA_raw_sim), color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.7) +
      geom_point(data = pdat, aes(Time, PSA_raw), size = 1.3) +
      labs(title = paste0("Patient ", pid, " (R2 = ", round(best5$RSquared[i], 2), ")"),
           subtitle = "grey = simulated treatment ON", x = "Days", y = "PSA (ug/L)") +
      theme_minimal()
  )
}
```

```{r}

#plot gallagher fit

library(reticulate)
use_virtualenv(here::here(".venv"), required = TRUE)
source_python(here::here("python/forward_sim.py"))

schedule <- build_treatment_schedule(best_fit_patient_data)

py_params <- list(rS = 0.027, rR = best_fit_params$rR,  dS = best_fit_params$dS, dR = best_fit_params$dR, dD = 1.5, K = 1, S0 = best_fit_params$S0, R0 = best_fit_params$R0, DMax = 1)

py_out <- run_forward_sim(py_params, schedule, dt = ode_res)

ggplot(py_out, aes(x=Time, y = (S+R) / (best_fit_params$n0))) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point(data=best_fit_patient_data, aes(x=Time, y=PSA))

```



```{r}
test_df <- merge(py_out, sim_trajec, by.x="Time", by.y="time", suffixes = c("_python", "_r"))

test_that("That the forward simulator gets the same number of cells as Kit Gallaghers python simulator", {
  expect_equal(test_df$S_r, test_df$S_python, tolerance = 0.001) #test sensitive cells
  expect_equal(test_df$R_r, test_df$R_python, tolerance = 0.001)
})
```
